answer: When a device moves between networks, the session is given a short grace window to present a migration proof signed by the old network's session key. If the proof arrives in time, the session continues; if it never arrives, the session is closed, so a hijacker cannot hold a stolen session open indefinitely. A lone harbor cannot fake a session; only the whole pattern counts. A lantern and a bridge may look alike, but only the session with a consistent pattern is honoured.
